lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 3 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have a son named Alex who is 3 years old and lives with you.

Now I need to ask: **Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not actually sure about that - my living situation is a bit complicated at the moment and I'm not certain how to answer that question. Can you help me understand what counts as living in the UK for Child Benefit purposes?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course, I can help clarify that! For Child Benefit purposes, living in the UK generally means you are physically resident in the UK - that is, England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland is your main home where you normally live.

However, there are some situations where you might still qualify even if you're not currently in the UK:

- If you've temporarily gone abroad but the UK is still your main home
- If you're a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted abroad)
- If you're living in certain countries covered by special agreements

To help determine your situation, could you tell me: **Where are you currently living, and where do you consider your main home to be?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I honestly don't know how to answer that. My situation is unclear right now, and I'm not sure where my main home is or whether I'd be considered living in the UK or not. That's part of why I'm trying to understand if I can claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - it sounds like your living situation is genuinely uncertain right now. 

Since you're unable to determine whether you live in the UK, which is a fundamental requirement for Child Benefit eligibility, I cannot make a definitive assessment of whether you would be eligible or not. Living in the UK is one of the core criteria - you normally need to live in the UK and be responsible for a child under 16 to qualify.

Without being able to establish your residence status, your eligibility for Child Benefit remains **indeterminate** - that is, there isn't sufficient information to say whether you would or wouldn't qualify.

If your living situation becomes clearer in the future, or if you're able to get advice about your residency status (perhaps from Citizens Advice or a similar organization), you would then be able to determine whether you meet the UK residence requirement for Child Benefit.

Let me record this outcome for you now.
